title: Christ the Priest
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Christ the Priest means that Jesus represents His people before God, offers the perfect sacrifice, and brings sinners near through His own blood. He is the great High Priest who saves completely.
summary: Christ the Priest means that Jesus represents His people before God, offers the perfect sacrifice, and brings sinners near through His own blood. He is the great High Priest who saves completely.
christFocus: Jesus is both the Priest and the sacrifice. He offered Himself once for all, entered the heavenly presence for His people, and continues to intercede with mercy and power.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Priests were appointed to represent people before God, offer sacrifices, and serve in the things of God. Christ fulfills and surpasses this ministry as the eternal High Priest.

Jesus does not offer the blood of animals. He offers Himself. His sacrifice is once for all, sufficient to cleanse the conscience and open the way into God’s presence.

Christ’s priesthood is also merciful. Because He became man and was tempted without sin, He sympathizes with weakness and invites His people to draw near to the throne of grace.

His priestly work continues. He lives forever and intercedes for those who draw near to God through Him. His people are not left without representation before the Father.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Sinners need more than encouragement to approach God. They need a Priest who can deal with guilt, cleanse sin, and bring them near to the holy God.

This doctrine gives confidence to ashamed, weak, and weary believers. Their access to God rests not on emotional strength or religious performance, but on Christ’s priestly work.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Draw near to God through Jesus your great High Priest. Do not stay away because of shame, weakness, or fear. Come through His blood, receive mercy, and depend on His ongoing intercession.
